query: AMETEK (AME) determines rev rec timing & control transfer indicators based on the terms of the sale, shipping terms, & transfer of risks & rewards.

For a small percentage of sales where title and risk of loss transfer at the point of delivery, revenue is recognized upon delivery, which is when control transfers, provided all other criteria are met. For certain contracts, particularly involving custom-made equipment or service repairs, revenue is recognized over time if the product has no alternative use and AMETEK has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date. In these cases, progress is typically measured using the cost-to-cost input method or, in some contracts, labor hours, to depict the transfer of control as work is performed. In summary, AMETEK uses the specific contract and shipping terms, along with the transfer of legal title, risks, and rewards, to determine when control is transferred and revenue should be recognized.

query: Contract asset vs notes receivable in T's rev rec installment programs.
final_answer: In AT&T's revenue recognition for wireless device sales under installment payment programs, the distinction between contract assets and notes receivable is as follows: - **Notes Receivable**: When a customer purchases a device on an installment plan and the devices are not discounted (i.e., sold at full standalone selling price) and AT&T's right to consideration is unconditional, revenue for the allocated portion is recognized at the point of sale. The difference between revenue recognized and consideration received is recorded as a note receivable. - **Contract Asset**: If the installment sale includes promotional discounts that are earned by the customer over the contract term (such as "buy one get one free" or equipment discounts with trade-in), notes receivable are recognized net of these discounts. The difference between revenue recognized and consideration received (after discounts) is recorded as a contract asset, which is then amortized over the contract term. - **Summary**: - Notes receivable are used when the right to payment is unconditional and there is no discount. - Contract assets arise when revenue is recognized but the consideration is conditional (such as when discounts are earned over time), and these assets are amortized over the duration of the contract. query: TPR's (Tapestry, Inc.) gift card liability breakage impact on revenue/prof profitability amid changing redemption patterns.

This recognition of breakage increases reported revenue and, consequently, can positively impact profitability. The company relies on historical information to estimate breakage. If redemption patterns change—such as more customers redeeming gift cards than historically expected—Tapestry would recognize less breakage revenue, potentially decreasing revenue and profitability. Conversely, if fewer cards are redeemed than anticipated, more breakage revenue would be recognized, increasing both revenue and profitability. The liability for unredeemed gift cards is recorded until redemption or until breakage is recognized. For the fiscal year ended June 29, 2024, deferred revenue related primarily to unredeemed gift cards was $45.5 million (up from $43.0 million in the prior year), and $27.7 million in net sales was recognized from amounts previously recorded as deferred revenue, reflecting the impact of gift card redemptions and breakage on revenue. In summary, gift card breakage provides a source of revenue for Tapestry, and shifts in customer redemption behavior will directly affect both the timing and amount of revenue and profit recognized from breakage.
